transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I'm here because I've been feeling completely exhausted and worn out all the time. I've also been struggling with this constant, overwhelming worry that I just can't seem to shake. It's been going on like this for about nine months now.
Did these symptoms start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or did they come on without a clear trigger? Have they been present most days for the full nine months?
They seemed to come on gradually without any clear trigger or major life change. And yes, they have definitely been present almost every single day for the entire nine months.

During these nine months, have you also felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day, or has the main problem been the constant worry? Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

The main problem has definitely been the constant worry, rather than feeling down or depressed. I haven't really lost interest in the things I enjoy, but the anxiety and worry are just so overwhelming and cause me the most distress.

Along with the constant worry, have you been having symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, muscle tension, trouble concentrating, irritability, or problems sleeping? Which of these have been happening most days?

I definitely have severe muscle tension, especially a stiff neck and shoulders, jaw clenching, and constant body aches. My concentration is also really poor because my mind gets tired easily and worries constantly intrude, though I don't really feel restless, irritable, or have trouble sleeping. These muscle stiffness and concentration issues happen almost every single day.
Do you find the worrying hard to control, and is it about many different areas of life like work, health, finances, or family rather than just one main issue?

Yes, I find it incredibly difficult to control; once the worrying starts, I just can't seem to stop it no matter how hard I try to distract myself. It's definitely not limited to one thing either, as I constantly worry about everything from my job and finances to my family's well-being.
